target.title: fix: surface cron errors for empty isolated agent replies
target.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query
-->

Closes #100162

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron-driven embedded agent runs could appear completed even when the final assistant turn produced no deliverable reply, leaving the configured channel without a response or failure signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron finalization now treats a delivery-requested embedded run with no final payload or synthesized text as a cron run error instead of passing it into the silent delivery path. The guard preserves intentional silent replies, message-tool/source deliveries that already satisfied the target, and committed terminal progress such as deterministic approval prompts, accepted child sessions, or successful cron adds, so this does not change explicit no-reply, already-delivered, approval-pending, or handoff-only flows.

## User Impact

Operators and channel users now get an observable cron failure state for empty final assistant completions instead of a dark lane where the job is marked complete but no reply reaches the destination.

## Evidence

- Added focused regressions for a completed embedded run with delivery requested and no final payload. They assert the plain empty completion and unverified/off-target message-tool attempts become `error` with no dispatch, while deterministic approval prompts, accepted child-session handoffs, and successful cron-add completions are not misclassified as cron errors.
- Focused regression passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.meta-error-status.test.ts` (10 tests).
- Near-real cron proof passed using qa-lab with qa-channel, a real gateway child process, and the mock-openai provider. The proof forced a delivery-requested isolated cron run whose mock model exhausted into an empty visible response; the run log showed `status=error`, `delivery=not-delivered`, and the qa-channel received one failure notification instead of the normal `EMPTY-EXHAUSTED-OK` success reply.
- Live cron proof passed using qa-lab with qa-channel, a real gateway child process, and live-frontier `claude-cli/opus`. The run stored a one-minute cron reminder, forced execution, completed via the cron path, and observed the QA channel delivery marker `QA-CRON-5df256c5`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed.

target.title: fix(codex): isolated cron reports Codex startup stalls
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

The root cause fixed here is a Codex app-server startup lifecycle timeout boundary: OpenClaw started the outer startup watchdog before Codex `initialize`, but the shared/isolated Codex client startup path did not receive the remaining startup deadline for that first required protocol request. When `client.initialize()` stalled after earlier startup work had consumed time, the broader startup watchdog could win first and surface a generic startup / isolated cron setup timeout instead of the blocked Codex initialize phase.

Why does this matter now?

For isolated cron runs routed through Codex, a stall before `thread/start` can currently look like `isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`, which hides the protocol phase that actually owns the failure once startup has reached `initialize`. The reporter's #84567 evidence proves the user-visible isolated cron setup timeout, `openai/gpt-5.5` / Codex routing, and a live idle Codex worker; it does not by itself prove the reporter-account run was already inside `client.initialize()`. The older #64744 evidence plus the deterministic proofs here cover the specific initialize lifecycle boundary.

What is the intended outcome?

Root-cause lifecycle fix for the Codex initialize timeout boundary: carry the startup deadline into the Codex app-server client factory, consume it only around `client.initialize()`, let the initialize timeout win before the outer watchdog, and stop connection-closed retries after the startup watchdog has already abandoned the attempt.

What is intentionally out of scope?

This does not change live OAuth auth selection, model routing, successful Codex app-server startup behavior, post-`thread/start` turn execution, user config, schema, protocol payloads, or public APIs. It also does not claim a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn.

What does success look like?

For runs that have reached Codex `initialize`, a stalled initialize request fails as `codex app-server initialize timed out` before `thread/start`, while pre-initialize factory/start-context hangs still report the generic startup timeout and successful initialize paths keep their existing behavior.

What should reviewers focus on?

Review the root invariant and risk boundary: `initialize` is the first required Codex protocol request before `thread/start`, so the remaining startup deadline must be enforced at that lifecycle owner instead of being left to a later generic startup watchdog. The timeout/retry change is intentionally narrow: only `client.initialize()` consumes the derived deadline, and connection-closed retries stop only after startup has already been abandoned.

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause Codex startup lifecycle and diagnostic-boundary fix for the `initialize` phase.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the pre-`thread/start` initialize stall boundary and the issue-shaped isolated cron runner route. Remaining external proof is a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn; this body states that boundary instead of claiming it.
- **Root cause:** OpenClaw's Codex startup owner created a single outer startup deadline, but the shared/isolated client startup owner did not receive that remaining deadline for the first Codex protocol request, `client.initialize()`. That mismatch let the generic startup watchdog own failures that had already reached the initialize lifecycle boundary.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch moves timeout ownership to the source lifecycle owner by passing an initialize deadline through the internal client factory options and consuming it only at `client.initialize()`. That fixes the root invariant that the first protocol request must complete or fail inside the existing startup budget, rather than masking the symptom after a generic cron setup timeout has already been reported.
- **Patch quality notes:** Timeout/retry changes are bounded: the initialize deadline is only consumed by the shared/isolated `client.initialize()` phase, callers that omit it keep the old factory-wide timeout behavior, pre-initialize factory hangs stay on the generic startup-timeout path, and retries stop only after the outer startup watchdog has abandoned startup.
- **What did NOT change:** OAuth profile selection, provider/model routing, successful Codex app-server startup, post-`thread/start` runtime behavior, public config, schema, protocol payloads, and public APIs.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth boundary is the Codex app-server lifecycle contract: `initialize` must complete before `thread/start`. OpenClaw now enforces the existing startup budget at that protocol lifecycle boundary instead of post-processing downstream cron setup errors.
- **Target test file:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** The regression suite locks the stalled real-stdio initialize boundary, the pre-initialize generic startup-timeout boundary, abandoned-startup cleanup, connection-closed retry ownership after abandonment, and the real isolated cron `agentTurn` route for `openai/gpt-5.5` with the `openai-codex:default` profile id.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The production change is limited to internal startup deadline wiring and retry ownership; the new cron proof uses the real isolated cron runner plus a Codex app-server protocol harness to exercise the issue-shaped route deterministically without requiring reporter-only OAuth credentials.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

This PR is related to #84567 and #64744. It does not use an auto-closing keyword because #84567 still has a reporter-account live OAuth cron/provider proof gap.

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #84567 and #64744. #84567 is the isolated cron setup-timeout report; #64744 provides older Codex initialize-hang context.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No direct maintainer request; this is a focused root-cause repair for linked bug reports and ClawSweeper review signals.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Stalled real stdio Codex initialize is bounded before `thread/start` and reports the initialize phase error.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node `v22.22.0`, OpenClaw worktree after this patch, with a real stdio child process spawned through the Codex app-server client startup path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
pnpm exec tsx <evidence>/real-stdio-stalled-initialize-proof.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):** copied output from the real-stdio proof:

```text

Real environment tested: Linux Node v22.22.0; spawned /usr/local/node/bin/node <evidence>/stalled-codex-app-server.mjs
Exact steps or command run after this patch: pnpm exec tsx evidence/real-stdio-stalled-initialize-proof.ts
Evidence after fix: observed error "codex app-server initialize timed out" after 9855 ms; onStartupTimeoutCalls=0; copied stub log lines are included below
Observed result after fix: initialize phase error won; generic codex app-server startup timed out was not surfaced.
What was not tested: a live OpenAI OAuth account or real Codex binary responding successfully after initialize.
```

Copied stub log from the real stdio child:

```text
2026-06-02T15:13:51.604Z stub-start pid=<redacted>
2026-06-02T15:13:51.609Z received method=initialize id=1
2026-06-02T15:14:00.757Z stub-exit signal=stdin-end
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The stdio child received the real `initialize` request, did not answer, OpenClaw raised `codex app-server initialize timed out`, and the generic `codex app-server startup timed out` message did not win.
- **What was not tested:** The stalled-stdio proof does not use a live OAuth account; it uses a deterministic real-stdio stalled app-server child to exercise the same pre-`thread/start` initialize boundary without external credentials.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** A full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn is still not claimed. The reporter's #84567 live/idle worker evidence proves the user-visible setup-timeout route but does not by itself prove the exact stall was inside `client.initialize()`.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged):** #64744 reported that a manually driven child could answer JSON-RPC `initialize` quickly while OpenClaw's `CodexAppServerClient.initialize()` promise did not resolve; #84567 reported recurring isolated cron setup timeout with a live/idle Codex worker.

Additional isolated cron proof:

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The real isolated cron `agentTurn` runner path for `openai/gpt-5.5` selects the Codex harness, preserves the user-selected `openai-codex:default` auth profile id, attributes an initialize stall to the Codex app-server initialize phase, and reaches `thread/start` after a successful initialize response.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node/Vitest cron test runner, OpenClaw worktree after this patch, real `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` execution path, and an in-memory Codex app-server protocol harness. The auth fixture uses a token-backed local credential for the `openai-codex:default` profile id with canonical provider `openai`; it does not claim a live reporter OAuth refresh.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts --testTimeout 60000 --reporter verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):** copied output from the isolated cron proof validation after rebasing onto current `origin/main`:

```text

 ✓ |cron| src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn Codex harness routing > attributes a Codex initialize stall from the selected harness to agent-run diagnostics 18158ms
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn Codex harness routing > uses the Codex harness for a successful isolated cron agentTurn 1074ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Start at  22:38:29
   Duration  33.54s (transform 24.66s, setup 894ms, import 13.12s, tests 19.24s, environment 0ms)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The isolated cron route selected the Codex app-server harness, preserved the `openai-codex:default` profile id, reported the stalled-initialize diagnostic before `thread/start`, and completed the successful `initialize` -> `thread/start` path in the same runner.
- **What was not tested:** This proof does not execute a live model turn, a real recurring cron fire against the reporter's account, or a live reporter OAuth refresh.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** The remaining proof question is maintainer acceptance of lifecycle/root-cause boundary evidence versus requiring a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.test.ts`
  - Result after rebasing onto current `origin/main`: 2 files passed, 35 tests passed.

```text
 RUN  v4.1.7 [local path redacted]

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
   Start at  22:37:26
   Duration  38.19s (transform 26.18s, setup 938ms, import 29.75s, tests 7.24s, environment 0ms)
```

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts --testTimeout 60000 --reporter verbose`
  - Result after rebasing onto current `origin/main`: 1 file passed, 2 tests passed.

```text
 RUN  v4.1.7 [local path redacted]

 ✓ |cron| src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn Codex harness routing > attributes a Codex initialize stall from the selected harness to agent-run diagnostics 18158ms
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn Codex harness routing > uses the Codex harness for a successful isolated cron agentTurn 1074ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Start at  22:38:29
   Duration  33.54s (transform 24.66s, setup 894ms, import 13.12s, tests 19.24s, environment 0ms)
```

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-factory.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts`
  - Result from the earlier proof round: no lint findings.
- `pnpm exec tsx <evidence>/real-stdio-stalled-initialize-proof.ts`
  - Result from the earlier proof round: copied in **Real behavior proof** above.
- `node --import tsx <evidence>/live-codex-oauth-setup-proof.mjs`
  - Result from the earlier proof round: managed Codex app-server completed `initialize`, returned idle `thread/start`, and no model turn was started.

What regression coverage was added or updated?

Added/updated regression coverage for stalled real-stdio initialize timeout attribution, remaining startup budget calculation, pre-initialize factory timeout boundary, startup-timeout cleanup, cancellation cleanup, startup RPC timeout behavior, connection-closed retry ownership after abandonment, and the isolated cron `agentTurn` route for `openai/gpt-5.5` via the Codex harness.

What failed before this fix, if known?

Before this fix, a stalled initialize after earlier startup work could let the broader startup watchdog surface a generic app-server startup / isolated cron setup timeout before the Codex initialize lifecycle owner reported `codex app-server initialize timed out`.

If no test was added, why not?

Tests were added and updated.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. For Codex startup attempts that reach `initialize` and then stall, the user-visible diagnostic changes from a generic startup/setup timeout to `codex app-server initialize timed out`.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

Availability during Codex app-server startup, because timeout ordering and connection-closed retry ownership changed around the first protocol request.

How is that risk mitigated?

The root-cause mitigation is scoped to the existing startup budget: startup passes an initialize deadline with a 150ms head start so the shared/isolated `client.initialize()` timeout can win before the outer watchdog. The optional internal factory field is only set by the Codex attempt startup path; callers that omit it keep previous timeout behavior. Pre-initialize factory/start-context hangs still use the generic startup timeout path, and connection-closed retries stop only after the startup watchdog has already abandoned the attempt. Focused tests and ClawSweeper review both covered this boundary.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Maintainer review after remote checks settle on the rebased head.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

No known local author action remains after this update. The PR branch is rebased onto current `origin/main` as a single commit; the previous conflict with `main` was limited to `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts` and is resolved by keeping `main`'s shorter 500ms test budget for the abandoned in-flight thread request while preserving the PR's initialize-deadline behavior and existing proof boundaries. Maintainers still need to decide whether the deterministic local isolated cron proof plus the real-stdio stalled initialize proof plus the live local OAuth Codex app-server setup proof are sufficient lifecycle/root-cause boundary evidence, or whether a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth isolated cron/provider turn is required before treating #84567 as fully root-caused. This update does not claim a model turn or recurring cron fire on the reporter account, and it does not claim that the reporter's live/idle worker snapshot alone proves the hang was inside `client.initialize()`.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

- **RF-001:** Maintainer-decision/proof-boundary item. The PR still discloses the user-visible diagnostic change and leaves final acceptance of the initialize-timeout ownership tradeoff to maintainers.
- **RF-002:** Maintainer-decision/proof-boundary item. The connection-closed retry behavior remains limited to startup already abandoned by the outer watchdog, with focused tests re-run after the rebase.
- **RF-003:** Disclosed proof limitation. This update still does not claim a full reporter-account live OpenAI OAuth recurring cron/provider turn.
- **RF-004:** Disclosed maintainer decision. The remaining question is proof sufficiency, not an additional code repair.
- **RF-005:** Re-run after rebasing onto current `origin/main`: focused app-server tests passed, 35 tests.
- **RF-006:** Re-run after rebasing onto current `origin/main`: `isolated-agent.codex-app-server.test.ts` passed, 2 tests.
- **RF-007:** Still covered by the earlier real-stdio stalled-initialize proof; this update preserved that lifecycle boundary and re-ran the focused app-server/cron validations.

target.title: feat(channels): expose source actor attribution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.
- Exports `SourceActorContext` and `SourceActorRole` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 and `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies.

## Production impact

No behavior change by itself. The change gives prompts, tools, and memory integrations a stable way to distinguish a group participant from the operator/user. Signal direct and group senders are represented as `participant` source actors.

## Evidence

- Channel context tests cover generic `SourceActor` projection and object-to-scalar mirror parity.
- Channel contract helpers now assert `SourceActor` scalar mirrors stay in sync with the canonical structured object.
- Signal mention-gating tests cover Signal sender identity mapping into the generic context.
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `SourceActor*` parity with production inbound context.
- Focused tests passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Plugin SDK API check passed without a baseline hash diff:
  `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Redacted Runtime Proof

Temporary local proof harness imported production `buildChannelInboundEventContext` and printed the emitted prompt context on PR head `5fab61f873`. The proof preserves the emitted source-actor shape while replacing all Signal identifiers, group identifiers, participant names, phone numbers, UUIDs, and message bodies with placeholders.

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<redacted proof harness>'
runtime-proof:environment
{
  "pr": 96863,
  "repo": "openclaw/openclaw",
  "head": "5fab61f873",
  "node": "v26.3.0"
}
runtime-proof:#96863 source actor fields emitted by prompt context
{
  "SourceActor": {
    "id": "signal:<redacted-phone>",
    "peerId": "signal:<redacted-uuid>",
    "displayName": "<redacted-display-name>",
    "role": "participant",
    "context": "signal-group:<redacted>"
  },
  "SourceActorId": "signal:<redacted-phone>",
  "SourceActorPeerId": "signal:<redacted-uuid>",
  "SourceActorDisplayName": "<redacted-display-name>",
  "SourceActorRole": "participant",
  "SourceActorContext": "signal-group:<redacted>",
  "scalarMirrorMatches": {
    "id": true,
    "peerId": true,
    "displayName": true,
    "role": true,
    "context": true
  }
}
```

### Operational Signal group evidence (2026-06-26)

A private Signal group smoke was run after a production config hotfix that kept the group-bound agent responding without changing Docker permissions. The private runtime intentionally stayed on its deployed OpenClaw release instead of being advanced to this PR stack today; the facts below are operational evidence for the real Signal group route, not an additional claim that this PR head is live-deployed.

Sanitized facts:

target.title: Add per-agent sandbox session visibility override feature
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: sandboxed session tools always applied the default sandbox session visibility clamp before considering the requesting agent, so `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` could be configured but was not consistently honored.
- Runtime impact: operators could not safely give one named sandboxed agent full configured session visibility while keeping other sandboxed agents clamped to spawned sessions.
- Change: session visibility resolution now derives the requester agent first, checks that agent's sandbox override, and falls back to `agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` only when no per-agent override exists.
- Compatibility: existing configs keep the same default `"spawned"` clamp unless a named agent explicitly sets `sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility`.

## User-Visible Behavior

New optional per-agent config:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "spawned" }
    },
    "list": [
      { "id": "tony", "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "all" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

For sandboxed session tools, precedence is:

```text
agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
default spawned clamp
```

## Security Impact

- Data access scope can broaden only for an explicitly named sandboxed agent.
- The global/default sandbox behavior remains clamped to spawned sessions.
- Existing `tools.sessions.visibility` and `tools.agentToAgent` policy checks still apply; this does not bypass cross-agent policy.
- No secrets, credentials, network calls, shell execution, or gateway auth behavior changed.

## Files in This PR

- `CHANGELOG.md` - records the user-facing runtime/config behavior change.
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md` - documents per-agent sandbox session visibility.
- `docs/gateway/config-tools.md` - documents session tool visibility and sandbox override precedence.
- `docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md` - documents multi-agent sandbox session tool behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` - wires requester identity into session tool construction.
- `src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware sandbox visibility to `session_status`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts` - centralizes requester-aware sandbox visibility resolution.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts` - forwards requester context through shared session helper wiring.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_history`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_list`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_send`.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts` - covers requester-aware `session_status` behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts` - covers tool-factory wiring for the override.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` - covers end-to-end session tool behavior through the OpenClaw tool factory.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts` - covers access-layer override/fallback resolution.

## Verification

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=360000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=dot`
  - Result: 10 test files passed, 268 tests passed.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: a sandboxed named agent with `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility="all"` can use the configured `tools.sessions.visibility` scope, while sandboxed agents without that override remain clamped to spawned sessions.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout using production `createOpenClawTools`, embedded OpenClaw gateway session handlers, and real temporary `sessions.json` stores for `main` and `tony`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e <inline proof script>` from the repo root. The script created an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, wrote real per-agent session stores, enabled embedded mode, constructed sandboxed `sessions_list` tools for `main` and `tony`, and compared observed session keys with expected visibility.

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "toolsSessionsVisibility": "all",
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] },
    "defaultSandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "spawned",
    "tonySandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "all"
  },
  "observed": {
    "mainSandboxedKeys": ["agent:main:subagent:main-child"],
    "tonySandboxedKeys": [
      "agent:main:main",
      "agent:main:subagent:main-child",
      "agent:tony:main",
      "agent:tony:subagent:tony-child"
    ]
  },
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

Observed result after fix: `main` stayed clamped to spawned sessions through the default sandbox setting; `tony` honored the per-agent `"all"` override and saw the full configured session scope when `tools.agentToAgent` allowed cross-agent access.

What was not tested: remote Crabbox/Testbox behavior. Crabbox is not installed in this shell, and the available Blacksmith CLI is unauthenticated.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk: an operator may grant broad session visibility to the wrong named agent.
- Mitigation: the override is explicit per agent, default behavior is unchanged, and cross-agent policy remains enforced.
- Rollback: remove `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` from the agent entry to return to the default sandbox clamp.

target.title: feat(android): syntax-highlighted code blocks in chat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fenced code blocks in Android chat render as flat monospace text, making code-heavy assistant replies hard to scan.

Part of #100195

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a minimal in-repo tokenizer (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatCodeHighlight.kt`) for kotlin/swift/typescript/javascript/python/bash/json with keyword/string/comment/number classes. An external highlighting library was evaluated and rejected: ~10 months without releases/commits, single maintainer, and no JSON support, versus ~300 lines of owned, testable code with no license-screen overhead. Token colors are new `MobileColors` code-palette slots (light+dark, ≥4.5:1 contrast against the code background). Streaming stays cheap: still-open fences render plain while a message streams (gated on CommonMark `closingFenceLength` + stream state), results are memoized per block content, and blocks over 200 lines or 20k chars fall back to plain rendering.

## User Impact

Assistant code blocks in chat get readable, theme-aware syntax coloring in light and dark mode. Unknown languages, streaming partial blocks, and very large blocks keep today's plain rendering. No config or behavior surface changes.

## Evidence

- `apps/android`: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests '*ChatMarkdown*' --tests '*AndroidLicenseNotices*'` — 20 tests, 0 failures (same green on `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest`)
- New tests in `ChatMarkdownTest.kt`: known-language tokens, theme span colors, unknown-language plain fallback, open-fence detection, line/char bounds incl. exact 200-line boundary, escaped quotes, bash comment boundaries, nested block comments, multiline template literals/shell strings
- Codex autoreview: 6 iterative rounds during development; 8 accepted findings fixed, each with a regression test; final run clean ("patch is correct", 0.88)

Known gap: unit-test proof only; no emulator screenshot pass of the rendered palette yet.

## What Problem This Solves

Memory recall can currently receive the conversation/session context without a stable indication of which group participant authored the triggering message. In multi-person channels, that can make retrieved or promoted memory read as if another participant's facts belong to the operator. This PR carries the generic source actor context into memory recall and prompt supplements so memory backends can preserve participant attribution without adding backend-specific logic.

## Summary

- Carries `SourceActor` from inbound context through embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Exposes the same source actor context to memory corpus supplements for `memory_search` and `memory_get`.
- Reuses the typed `SourceActorRole` contract across reply runtime, plugin tool context, and memory context.
- Adds memory prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution instead of merging another participant's facts into the operator/user profile.

## Scope and honesty

This PR carries `SourceActor` context into memory recall and adds prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution. It is the plumbing + guidance layer: it makes attribution available and instructs the model to keep it. It does NOT yet structurally enforce attribution on stored memories (e.g., tagging persisted entries with the source actor) -- that is a follow-up. Best-effort: recall tracking never blocks recall.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738, `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`, and `codex/source-actor-context-contract`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies. Merge order should stay #96738 -> #96862 -> #96863 -> #96864, with later PRs rebased after earlier ones land.

## Production impact

No storage migration and no backend-specific behavior. This is not Honcho-specific: it adds a generic runtime/tool/memory contract that memory backends and supplements can consume. ## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

## Summary

target.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files:
  - `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-roots.test.ts`
  - `src/media/load-options.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-media-access.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/images.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-pinned-write-helper.spawn-error.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.unlink-helper-error.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`
  - `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
  - `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots
  - roots precedence over `workspaceOnly` for host-mode FS access
  - sandbox-mode fallback still honoring `workspaceOnly`
  - rooted local image/PDF/reference-image loads outside the workspace
  - rooted outbound local-media and reply-delivery paths preserving file-vs-dir root semantics
  - rooted prompt-image auto-load outside the workspace
  - host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations (TOCTOU-safe)
  - sandboxed outbound media delivery ignores configured host roots
  - rooted delete helper gracefully falls back when pinned write helper spawn fails
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the risky surfaces here are policy resolution, host-path mutation, and media path propagation, so targeted seam tests catch the actual failure modes without requiring a full live deployment.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New config surface: `tools.fs.roots` on global `tools.fs` and per-agent `tools.fs`.
- Operators can now grant read-only or read-write access to specific directories/files outside the workspace without granting full host filesystem access.
- Host-mode `read` / `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` now respect those explicit roots.
- Local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery flows, and prompt-image auto-load now preserve and enforce rooted file/dir access semantics.
- When both `roots` and `workspaceOnly` are set, `roots` takes precedence for host-mode FS access and a warning is logged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - This adds a new operator-controlled path restriction model for host-mode FS access. Risk is policy misunderstanding or incomplete enforcement across FS-adjacent surfaces. Mitigation: all configured roots are validated as absolute paths; enforcement is alias-safe; canonical root precedence is preserved for host-mode mutation paths; host-mode `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load are covered; host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations to close TOCTOU gaps; sandbox mode explicitly ignores roots to avoid host/container path confusion.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15 / darwin 25.3.0
- Runtime/container: local repo checkout
- Model/provider: N/A for core FS policy; targeted local media tests use mocked image/PDF/image-generation providers
- Integration/channel (if any): host-mode FS tools + local media loading + outbound local-media reply flows
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json5
{
  "tools": {
    "fs": {
      "roots": [
        { "path": "/opt/app/workspaces/agent-1", "kind": "dir", "access": "rw" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/invoices", "kind": "dir", "access": "ro" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/context.md", "kind": "file", "access": "ro" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Steps

1. Configure an agent with `tools.fs.roots` containing a writable workspace root and one or more external host paths.
2. Attempt `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` and local media access both inside and outside those roots.
3. Attempt outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows with both dir roots and exact file roots.
4. Attempt prompt-image auto-load from a rooted external image path.
5. Attempt the same config in sandbox mode.

### Expected

- Host-mode FS and local media access succeed only within configured roots, respecting `ro` vs `rw`.
- Outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows preserve file-vs-dir root semantics and explicit deny-all behavior.
- Prompt-image auto-load accepts explicitly rooted host paths.
- Sandbox mode ignores `roots` and continues to rely on Docker isolation plus `workspaceOnly` fallback behavior.

### Actual

- Before this change, there was no granular host-path policy between workspace-only and unrestricted host access.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified on the current merged head (`7b771d448d`):
  - merged `origin/main` at `631552c554`
  - `pnpm config:docs:gen`
  - `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`
  - `pnpm check`
  - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.memory-flush-forwarding.test.ts`
  - `pnpm test src/media/read-capability.test.ts`
  - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/media/read-capability.test.ts src/media/local-roots.test.ts`

  - `pnpm test src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts -t "sends transcriptPrompt visibly and queues runtime context as hidden custom context"`
  - `pnpm test src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts -t "ignores host roots for sandboxed read/write/edit tools"`
- Additional focused regressions were exercised during review for:
  - fs-root resolution / precedence
  - alias-safe host mutations and unlink/delete behavior
  - media root propagation and explicit deny-all handling
  - prompt-image and local-media rooted access
  - outbound local-media / reply-delivery adapters
  - pinned-FD host reads (TOCTOU closure)

- What you did **not** verify on `7b771d448d`:
  - full local `pnpm test`
  - `pnpm build`
  - live end-to-end multi-tenant deployment behavior beyond local seam tests
  - `pnpm check:changed` did not complete locally: it passed type/lint/guard phases and 2,450 tests before a local Vitest gateway worker hit `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: remove `tools.fs.roots` from config or revert this PR.
- Files/config to restore: `src/agents/pi-tools.ts`, `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.ts`, `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.ts`, `src/agents/apply-patch.ts`, media/local-root propagation files, and the config schema/help/generated baseline files.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: host-mode local media or prompt-image access unexpectedly denied for paths inside configured roots, rooted outbound attachments unexpectedly losing exact-file semantics, symlink delete/unlink behavior regressing at root boundaries, or sandbox-generated outbound attachments unexpectedly blocked when host-mode `tools.fs.roots` is configured.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a host-mode path surface could miss roots enforcement and create an unexpected gap.
  - Mitigation: added targeted regression tests for host tools, `apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Risk: operator confusion when both `workspaceOnly` and `roots` are present.
  - Mitigation: `roots` precedence is explicit in schema/help and a runtime warning is logged.
- Risk: `exec` still bypasses FS roots through shell commands.
  - Mitigation: documented as an intentional scope boundary; deployments needing hard FS boundaries should not allow `exec`.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI-assisted
- Testing: locally revalidated on the current merged head (`7b771d448d`) with `pnpm check`, focused media/WhatsApp review-thread regressions, and the two prior PR-specific filtered tests; full `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` were not rerun on this final merged head; GitHub CI is green on `7b771d448d` (74 successful, 9 skipped) after the latest review fix.




## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `tools.fs.roots` lets an operator grant an agent narrowly-scoped host filesystem access — an allowlist of roots, each `dir`/`file` with `ro`/`rw` access. Host-mode read/write/edit (and apply_patch) must allow paths inside an allowed root, deny paths outside every root, and reject writes to `ro` roots.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at PR head `b4056fc332` (Node 22, macOS), driving the production host-mode filesystem tools against a real on-disk temporary directory tree (real `fs` syscalls; no fixtures or stubs).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created a real temp tree (an `rw` root `shared-rw`, an `ro` root `shared-ro`, and a `secret/` directory outside every root with a real file in it), built the production tool set via `createOpenClawCodingTools({ config: { tools: { fs: { roots: [...] } } } })`, and executed the resulting `read`/`write` tools against each path with `node --import tsx`. Live console output below.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
config tools.fs.roots:
  - { path: /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-rw, kind: dir, access: rw }
  - { path: /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-ro, kind: dir, access: ro }
workspace (not a root): /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/workspace
forbidden dir (not a root): /tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/secret

=== host-mode reads ===
READ  inside rw root  (shared-rw/notes.txt)
      -> ALLOWED, content: "rw-root content"
READ  inside ro root  (shared-ro/policy.txt)
      -> ALLOWED, content: "ro-root content"
READ  OUTSIDE roots   (secret/passwords.txt)
      -> DENIED: Access denied: path '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/secret/passwords.txt' is outside allowed filesystem roots

=== host-mode writes ===
WRITE inside rw root  (shared-rw/created.txt)
      -> ALLOWED, on disk: true
WRITE inside ro root  (shared-ro/hack.txt)
      -> DENIED: Access denied: path '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-ro/hack.txt' is inside read-only root '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/shared-ro'  (on disk: false)
WRITE OUTSIDE roots   (secret/exfil.txt)
      -> DENIED: Access denied: path '/tmp/fs-roots-proof-qTDt3u/secret/exfil.txt' is outside allowed filesystem roots  (on disk: false)

verify: secret/passwords.txt still says: "TOP SECRET — outside every allowed root"
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Reads inside the `rw` and `ro` roots returned the real file contents. A read of `secret/passwords.txt` (outside every root) was denied with `outside allowed filesystem roots`. A write inside the `rw` root landed on disk (`on disk: true`); a write to the `ro` root was denied (`inside read-only root`) and a write outside every root was denied — both left nothing on disk (`on disk: false`), and the out-of-root secret file was byte-for-byte unchanged afterward.
- **What was not tested:** Sandbox mode is out of scope by design — sandbox ignores `tools.fs.roots` and relies on Docker isolation — so it was not exercised here. No live LLM agent loop was run (no provider key in this environment); the proof drives the exact production tool layer the agent calls, against a real filesystem, rather than a full conversational turn.

target.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events
target.body:
### Summary

Add `rawBody` field to user messages in `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`, and `before_agent_start` (legacy) hook events. This provides plugins with the original user input before channel structural context, `buildInboundUserContextPrefix()` metadata, and prompt-build hook injections are prepended.

### Motivation

Plugin hooks receive `event.messages` where user message `content` includes OpenClaw-injected metadata (timestamps, channel info, sender IDs) and other hook injections (e.g., memory context). Plugins that process user content for purposes like memory extraction, summarization, or analytics must parse and strip this metadata — a fragile approach since the format varies by channel, chat type, and OpenClaw version.

PR #51502 already established the precedent of using `RawBody` instead of `Body` to avoid passing envelope metadata to LLM processing. This PR extends that principle to plugin hook events.

### Changes

- Compute `rawBodyForHooks` from `CommandBody ?? RawBody ?? Body` in the channel message handler — the clean user text without @mentions, sender labels, or message annotations
- Thread `rawBody` through the run params chain: `get-reply-run.ts` → `runReplyAgent` → `runAgentTurnWithFallback` → `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `runEmbeddedAttempt`
- Include `rawBody` in hook event objects for `before_prompt_build`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`
- Add `rawBody` to `FollowupRun` type so the value survives queueing/deferred runs
- `rawBody` is `undefined` for non-channel runs (CLI, heartbeat, cron)
- **Steer race fix** (`86ebda8b`): Thread `rawBody` through the steer queue path so steered injections on non-Telegram channels refresh the active embedded run's hook context

### Backward Compatibility

- Additive optional field only — no breaking changes
- Plugins can feature-detect `rawBody` and fall back to `content`:
  ```typescript
  const userText = event.rawBody ?? extractText(lastUser.content);
  ```
- Plugin SDK API baseline unchanged (no drift)

### Use Case

Memory plugins send user+assistant pairs to backend for memory extraction. Without `rawBody`, the plugin must regex-strip injected XML blocks and cannot remove inbound metadata, causing noisy "memories" from message IDs and timestamps. With `rawBody`, the plugin gets clean user input directly.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Plugin hook events (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`) now expose `event.rawBody` containing clean user-input text (22 chars) instead of requiring plugins to parse the metadata-decorated `messages[-1].content` (411 chars). Non-channel origins (heartbeat, cron, exec-event) correctly emit `rawBody: undefined`. Steered injections on non-Telegram channels now refresh `rawBody` via the steer queue path.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-1013-aws (arm64), Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.5.20, Bedrock `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (us-east-1, IAM role auth), Telegram bot `@oc_jmu_bot` via long-poll, custom probe plugin (`rawbody-probe`) using `definePluginEntry` + `api.on("before_prompt_build")` + `api.on("agent_end")`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built from PR HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` = `29e89cfb84`), ran `pnpm build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured --port 18799 --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`. Sent Telegram DM "hello rawbody test 004" to `@oc_jmu_bot`. Triggered heartbeat via `node openclaw.mjs system event --text "..." --mode now --url ws://127.0.0.1:18799 --token anonymous --json`. Ran unit tests: `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts -t "rawBody hook gating" --reporter=verbose`.

Evidence after fix:
```
Case A — Channel happy path (Telegram DM):
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 4c1c5a9b-8e2c-405f-b6f3-d2246e4912cc
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = user
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = "hello rawbody test 004"   (22 chars)
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n...
                            hello rawbody test 003"   (411 chars)
[rawbody-probe] equal    = false
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = prompt,messages,rawBody

Case B — Heartbeat origin:
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 40d31407-6882-4f23-bdc7-85ba18fb5a41
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = heartbeat
```

target.title: fix(cron): stop fallback attempts when cron budget is exhausted
target.body:
## Problem

When a cron job's primary model times out near the cron deadline, the fallback model is started but immediately killed by the same cron timeout — receiving effectively 0ms to make an LLM request. The fallback never gets a fair chance to respond, and the user sees a misleading `cron: job execution timed out` error attributed to the fallback model.

**Observed in production logs (2026-03-22):**

```
[08:10:30.733] anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 attempt=1/2 reason=unknown err='Request was aborted.' duration=28667ms
[08:10:30.735] openai-codex/gpt-5.4    attempt=2/2 reason=timeout err='cron: job execution timed out' duration=0ms
```

The cron timeout wraps the entire fallback chain. When the primary model consumes most of the budget, the fallback model is allocated ~0ms and fails immediately.

## Solution

1. **Propagate the cron deadline** (`deadlineAtMs`) from `executeJobCoreWithTimeout` through the cron service state down to `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`.

2. **Add a `beforeAttempt` hook** to `runWithModelFallback` that is called before each candidate attempt. If it returns `{ type: 'stop' }`, the fallback chain stops and preserves the original error from the previous attempt.

3. **Check remaining budget** in the cron layer's `beforeAttempt` callback. If less than `min(30s, timeout/4)` remains before the cron deadline, the fallback is skipped with a clear message:
   > `Skipping fallback: only 50ms remain before cron timeout (need at least 30000ms).`

This ensures:
- The primary model's real error is preserved (not masked by a fake cron timeout on the fallback)
- No wasted LLM API calls that would be aborted instantly
- The `beforeAttempt` hook is generic and reusable for other pre-attempt checks

## Changes

- `src/agents/model-fallback.ts` — Add `beforeAttempt` hook + `stop_before_candidate` decision type
- `src/cron/service/timer.ts` — Compute and pass `deadlineAtMs` to job execution
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` — Use `beforeAttempt` to check remaining cron budget
- `src/cron/service/state.ts` + `src/gateway/server-cron.ts` — Thread `deadlineAtMs` through interfaces

## Tests

- `model-fallback.test.ts` — beforeAttempt stop behavior
- `run.fallback-time-budget.test.ts` — Cron deadline propagation + fallback budget exhaustion
- `service.issue-regressions.test.ts` — Deadline passed to isolated runs


## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Cron isolated agent-turn jobs should not start a model fallback when the primary attempt has consumed almost the whole cron deadline and the fallback would be killed immediately by the same timeout.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/cron-fallback-timeout` at `008791fa10`, macOS host, Node 22. The proof command uses the same fallback budget formula added in this branch and the cron job shape from the affected isolated agent-turn surface.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `node .artifacts/pr-52365-real-behavior-proof.mjs` locally after the patch, then ran `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-time-budget.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` as supplemental coverage for the same gate.

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from the local reproduction command:

```
$ node .artifacts/pr-52365-real-behavior-proof.mjs
cron fallback budget repro
job: sessionTarget=isolated wakeMode=next-heartbeat payload=agentTurn timeoutSeconds=60
primary attempt: consumed 59900ms of a 60000ms cron deadline
fallback check: remainingMs=100; fallbackMinRemainingMs=15000
before(upstream/main): runWithModelFallback had no beforeAttempt budget gate -> fallbackAttempted=true
after(this branch): fallbackAttempted=false
after stop: Skipping fallback: only 100ms remain before cron timeout (need at least 15000ms).
```

Supplemental targeted test output:

```
$ pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-time-budget.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
✓ allows fallback attempts when the per-attempt budget fits inside the remaining cron deadline
✓ uses agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds for fallback budget when job timeoutSeconds is unset
✓ stops new fallback attempts when the per-attempt budget no longer fits
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Observed result after fix:** With only 100ms left before the cron deadline and a 15,000ms minimum fallback budget, the after-fix gate returns `fallbackAttempted=false` and reports `Skipping fallback: only 100ms remain before cron timeout (need at least 15000ms).` The before behavior had no `beforeAttempt` budget gate, so the fallback candidate was started even though it could only receive about 0ms.

**What was not tested:** Live Anthropic/OpenAI API calls were not run for this proof; the local reproduction covers the cron fallback budget decision and the targeted test covers the runtime hook path with mocked provider execution.

target.title: fix(agents): surface real plugin approval rejection reason to agent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100212: When the gateway rejects a plugin approval request (e.g. schema validation → `INVALID_REQUEST`), the agent receives a hardcoded "Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)" message. The gateway is actually healthy and actively rejected the request — the misleading message points debugging in the wrong direction.

**Real-world impact**: This misled operators at Clawnify.com during a production incident where an overlong approval title (98 chars, cap is 80) caused every mutating tool call to fail. The agent, seeing "gateway unavailable," concluded the target app was broken — while the gateway was perfectly healthy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catch block around the `plugin.approval.request` gateway call in `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts` returned a fixed string regardless of error type. Now we distinguish:

- **GatewayClientRequestError** (gateway code present) → `"Plugin approval request rejected: <real message>"` — gateway is up, request was invalid
- **Other errors** (connection refused, timeout, etc.) → `"Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)"` — genuine transport failure

## User Impact

- Agents and operators now see the real rejection reason, enabling faster root-cause analysis
- Gateway-unavailability detection still works correctly for actual transport failures
- Backward compatible: all existing tests pass unchanged

target.title: fix(infra): tolerate deleted cwd across startup, PATH, home-dir, and TUI [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #73676. If a shell's working directory is removed before OpenClaw starts, Node's `process.cwd()` throws `ENOENT: uv_cwd`. CLI dotenv/PATH bootstrap and TUI startup used that call directly, so `openclaw tui` terminated before it could render a useful interface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduce one small nullable-CWD primitive, then keep the decision at each owner boundary:

- dotenv skips the vanished workspace file and continues global loading;
- PATH setup skips the opt-in project-local bin lookup rather than substituting HOME;
- required-home resolution uses valid configured sources or fails with actionable guidance;
- TUI workspace inference skips a missing cwd, autocomplete/auth use the package-root fallback, and local `!` commands refuse instead of silently running somewhere else.

This maintainer rewrite removes the redundant `is-main` refactor, the extra helper/test-routing surface, and the long fallback comments from the contributor patch. Normal cwd-present behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

The CLI and full-screen TUI can start after their launch directory has been deleted. Security-sensitive project/PATH and local-shell semantics do not gain an implicit fallback. The unrecoverable no-home/no-cwd edge case now names the environment variables or directory action required.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwsmjrh13za4ghjn0kcrhfjt`, [run 28748684029](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28748684029): 147 focused boundary/dotenv/TUI tests passed on the final rebased source.

target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

target.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #51620 — gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages.

## Changes

### New: `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.ts`
Serializes all non-empty `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` entries to `state/pending-messages.json` before shutdown. Strips non-portable fields (`config`, `skillsSnapshot`) and stores a version marker + timestamp.

### New: `src/gateway/server-pending-messages.ts`
On startup, reads the persisted file, injects missed messages as system events into their respective sessions (so the agent processes them on next turn), then deletes the file. Includes a 5-minute staleness guard to avoid replaying ancient messages from stale files.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-close.ts`
Calls `persistFollowupQueues(FOLLOWUP_QUEUES)` before `chatRunState.clear()` so queue state is captured while still available. Best-effort — failure doesn't block shutdown.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-startup.ts`
Calls `replayPersistedPendingMessages()` 1.5s after startup (after channels initialize), alongside the existing `scheduleRestartSentinelWake`.

## Tests

16 new tests covering:
- `persistFollowupQueues`: empty queues, non-empty queues, config stripping, multiple queues
- `consumePersistedQueues`: no file, read+delete, staleness guard (>5min), corrupt file, wrong version
- Round-trip: persist → consume
- `replayPersistedPendingMessages`: no entries, empty entries, system event injection, multiple queues, prompt truncation, empty items skip

## Limitations / Follow-up

This PR covers **Phase 1**: persisting in-memory followup queue items across restart.

Still not covered (follow-up work):
- **Phase 2**: Messages arriving during the drain window (hitting `GatewayDrainingError`) — these are rejected at the channel level before reaching the queue
- **Phase 3**: Channel-level message acknowledgment deferral — for channels that support it (Slack Socket Mode), defer ACK until message is processed or persisted so the platform can redeliver

## Testing

```
npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.test.ts src/gateway/server-pending-messages.test.ts
```

All 16 tests pass.

target.title: feat(chat-ui): syntax-highlighted code blocks and native tables in chat markdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Assistant messages in the shared Apple chat UI rendered fenced code without syntax highlighting and GFM tables as raw pipe characters because the whole message went through one `AttributedString(markdown:)` / `Text` pass that does not provide either surface.

Part of #100195. Addresses the table portion of #98290.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer now uses Swift Markdown's GFM AST to extract only top-level fenced code and tables before display. Prose retains the existing `AttributedString` path, so list and HTML containers plus document-scoped reference links keep their CommonMark semantics. Completed fenced blocks use a bounded single-pass highlighter for Swift, Kotlin, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Bash, and JSON; unknown, incomplete, oversized, or overlong blocks stay readable and unstyled. Tables render with native SwiftUI cells, GFM alignment, escaped pipes, short-row padding, and explicit row, column, cell, and byte limits.

The parser dependency is pinned to Swift Markdown 0.8.0, the current stable Swift.org implementation backed by cmark-gfm. Direct Swift Markdown and cmark-gfm source inspection verified source-range, table-span, container, and reference-definition behavior. Splash is Swift-focused and inactive for this broader grammar set; Highlightr adds JavaScriptCore plus bundled highlight.js grammars/themes for a six-language chat subset. The bounded in-repo tokenizer therefore remains the smaller highlighting layer while the maintained parser owns Markdown structure.

The rewrite also removes the hand-maintained block parser, makes soft-break preservation AST-aware for nested and indented code, covers Swift/Kotlin nested comments and Bash parameter expansions/redirection boundaries, caps highlighting at 200 logical lines / 20,000 UTF-8 bytes, and includes the new shared sources in the generated iOS SwiftFormat input list.

## User Impact

iOS and macOS chat show readable syntax-highlighted code cards and native aligned tables. Streaming remains responsive, source text is preserved exactly, and light/dark palettes remain dynamic.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests|ChatCodeHighlighterTests|ChatMarkdownDisplayPreprocessorTests'` — 72/72 passed.
- `swift test -q --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit` — 321/321 passed.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --scratch-path /tmp/openclaw-macos-100207-ast-build` — passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

- Exposes Signal mention-gating facts on the generic inbound message context.
- Adds `CanDetectMention`, `HasAnyMention`, `RequireMention`, `EffectiveWasMentioned`, and `MentionSource` for delivered native/text mention decisions.
- Keeps the Signal mention source literal typed so SDK/context consumers can rely on `"native"` vs `"mention_pattern"`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. Skipped Signal turns still return before prompt/tool context is built, so this PR intentionally does not expose a public skipped-turn context field.

target.title: fix(agents): hint when unknown tools are skills
target.body: ## Summary - **Problem:** When a model mistakenly calls a skill name as a tool (e.g. `my-skill`), the error message is a generic "Tool not found" with no guidance, so the model keeps retrying or gives up. This is especially common with weaker/smaller models that struggle to distinguish skills from tools in the system prompt. - **Why it matters:** Skills are invoked differently from tools; without a hint the model has no way to self-correct, leading to repeated failed tool calls that waste tokens and frustrate users — particularly on cost-sensitive or lower-capability model configurations. - **What changed:** Register an `afterToolCall` hook in `attempt.ts` that intercepts error tool results, detects unknown-tool errors matching a registered skill name, and rewrites the message to `Tool "X" not found. "X" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` Also extracted `resolveUnknownToolName` helper in `errors.ts` (was inline regex) and exported `rewriteToolResultUnknownToolError` for the hook to call. - **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** `formatAssistantErrorText` signature and all its callers are untouched. No new params threaded through `run.ts`, `payloads.ts`, `subscribe.types.ts`, or lifecycle handlers. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Feature - [x] Refactor ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Skills / tool execution ## Linked Issue/PR None ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - When a model calls a skill name as a tool and the skill is registered, the error tool result now says: `Tool "X" not found. "X" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` - When the tool name does not match any registered skill, behavior is unchanged (generic "Tool not found"). ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0, arm64) - Runtime/container: Node 22 + pnpm - Model/provider: Claude (Anthropic) - Relevant config: workspace with registered skills (e.g. `my-skill`, `another-skill`) ### Steps 1. Start an OpenClaw agent session with skills registered 2. Prompt the model to call a skill name as if it were a tool (e.g. "use tool my-skill") 3. Observe the error tool result returned to the model ### Expected - Error message: `Tool "my-skill" not found. "my-skill" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` ### Actual - Confirmed: skill-matching errors get the hint; non-skill unknown tools get the generic error. ## Evidence - [x] Trace/log snippets Manually tested two scenarios: 1. Called skill names (`my-skill`, `another-skill`) as tools -> got skill hint message 2. Called nonexistent name (`banana123`) as tool -> got generic "Tool not found" ## Human Verification (required) - **Verified scenarios:** Both skill-match and non-match unknown tool errors in a live OpenClaw agent session. - **Edge cases checked:** Tool name that does not match any skill; empty skill snapshot; multiple registered skills. - **What you did not verify:** Behavior with the upstream pi-agent-core `immediate` branch change (afterToolCall on prepareToolCall); that path is covered by the pi-agent-core MR. ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks) - How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert commit `e527e3c111`; the `afterToolCall` hook is additive and removing it restores default unknown-tool errors. - Files/config to restore: `errors.ts`, `attempt.ts` - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: If `setAfterToolCall` is called before the agent session is fully initialized, the hook may not fire; watch for missing skill hints in logs. ## Risks and Mitigations - **Risk:** `rewriteToolResultUnknownToolError` regex may not match all provider error formats. - **Mitigation:** Uses the same regex patterns already proven in `formatAssistantErrorText`; additional patterns can be added to `resolveUnknownToolName` without changing the hook wiring.

target.title: fix(process): suppress unhandled stdout/stderr stream errors in runCommandWithTimeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runCommandWithTimeout` attaches `data` listeners to `child.stdout` and `child.stderr`, but does not attach `error` listeners. If either stream emits an `error` event (e.g., pipe read failure, premature close), the unhandled error can crash the process even though the command itself would otherwise complete normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add no-op `error` handlers to both stdout and stderr streams before the data handlers, mirroring the existing stdin EPIPE swallowing pattern. This prevents unhandled stream errors from propagating as uncaught exceptions.

## User Impact

More robust subprocess execution: transient stream read errors no longer crash the OpenClaw process.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/process/exec.test.ts` that emits `error` events on both stdout and stderr and verifies `runCommandWithTimeout` still resolves successfully.
- Verified the test fails on `main` with `Error: stdout read failed` and passes with this fix.
- `oxlint` passes on the changed files.
